items.stem: An office chair is priced at ₱480. It is sold at 15% off. How much does a buyer pay?

reveal.terms: "15% off" means 15 pesos less for every 100 pesos of the price.

why_wrong.o1: ₱72 is the discount itself. The buyer pays the price minus this amount.
why_wrong.o3: ₱465 subtracts 15 pesos, not 15% of the price.
why_wrong.o4: ₱552 adds 15% instead of taking it off.

items.shortcut: Move the decimal one place for 10% (₱48), halve it for 5% (₱24), and build 15% from those: ₱72 off, so ₱408.

items.micro_skill: find perimeter, then multiply by cost per meter
items.stem: A rectangular parking area is 22 m long and 7 m wide. Edging costs ₱40 per meter. How much will it cost to put the edging around the whole parking area?

reveal.terms: "Perimeter" is the distance around a shape. For a rectangle it is 2 × (length + width).

why_wrong.o1: This uses the area (154 square meters). Going around uses the perimeter.
why_wrong.o2: ₱58 is just the perimeter in meters written as pesos. It stops before multiplying by ₱40.
why_wrong.o4: This uses only one length and one width (29 m). A rectangle has two of each.

items.shortcut: Add length and width once, then double: 22 + 7 = 29, × 2 = 58 m. × ₱40 = ₱2,320.

items.stem: Statement 1: Some mangoes are exports. Statement 2: All mangoes are fruits. Which conclusion follows from both statements?

reveal.terms: A conclusion "must be true" only if the statements force it. Ignore what you know from real life.
reveal.shortcut: The mangoes that are exports are also fruits. So at least some fruits are exports.
reveal.why_correct: "Some fruits are exports." is right. It follows from the two statements with no extra facts.

why_wrong.o1: This contradicts the statements: the mangoes that are exports are also fruits.
why_wrong.o3: Only some of the mangoes are exports, so we cannot say all fruits are.
why_wrong.o4: This flips the statement about exports. Some exports may be outside the group.

items.stem: Nestor can paint a classroom in 21 hours. Aling Rosa can do the same job in 28 hours. Working together, how long will they take?

reveal.terms: A "rate" is how much of the job gets done in one hour.
reveal.shortcut: Per hour, Nestor does 1/21 and Aling Rosa does 1/28. Together: 1/21 + 1/28 = 1/12. So the whole job takes 12 hours.
reveal.why_correct: 12 hours is right. Check: in 12 hours, Nestor does 12/21 and Aling Rosa does 12/28; together that is 1 whole job.

why_wrong.o2: 24.5 hours is the average of the two times. Together they must be faster than the faster person alone.
why_wrong.o3: 49 hours adds the two times. Add the work done per hour, not the hours.
why_wrong.o4: 7 hours subtracts the two times (28 − 21). Add the work done per hour; do not subtract the hours.

items.shortcut: For two workers, time together = product ÷ sum: (21 × 28) ÷ (21 + 28) = 588 ÷ 49 = 12 hours.

revisions.change: Swapped the implausible '5 minutes' distractor for '7 hours', the difference of the two times.
